 Judgment

The petitioner claims to be the tenant of property owned by certain Sri.P.K.Shaji and that she is running a Jack fruit Processing Company therein, on the strength of a valid licence which had been issued by the 1 st respondent - Secretary of Adimali Grama Panchayat.
2.

According to the petitioner, after the petitioner leased the afore property, Sri.P.K.Shaji wanted to become her partner and that Ext.P2 partnership deed was thereafter drawn up, but that he was subsequently arraigned in two cases, registered by the Circle Inspector of Exercise,
Thiruvananthapuram, under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, numbered as Crime Nos.14/2018 and 19/2018.

entities.text: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
She says that, in the meanwhile, the Trade Licence with respect to her business expired and that when she applied for its renewal, it was rejected through Ext.P11 proceedings of the Secretary of the Panchayat, informing that the Trade Licence cannot be renewed for her business as long as she continues in the property in question, since they have already been notified by WP(C).No.16393 OF 2019(Y) the Assistant Exercise Commissioner,
Thiruvananthapuram, that it has been attached and frozen under the provisions of Section 68F(1) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act (NDPS Act for short).
3. The petitioner asserts that Ext.P11 is incompetent in law, since the proceedings under the NDPS Act cannot apply to a property but only to its owner; and that, in any event of the matter, since she is not involved in any of the said cases, she is willing to evict herself from the property as and when action against the property is taken by the competent Authorities under the provisions of the said Act.

entities.text: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: She, therefore, says that her application be directed to be reconsidered and the Panchayat be ordered to renew the Trade Licence immediately.

4. The learned Government Pleader - Sri.Manuraj K.J, appearing on behalf of the 2nd respondent - Assistant Excise Commissioner, submits that the owner of the property is a notorious offender and that he is involved in several cases apart from the two that have been mentioned by the petitioner in this writ petition.

He says that Ext.P10 proceedings have been issued by the Assistant Excise Commissioner invoking the WP(C).No.16393 OF 2019(Y) powers under Section 68F(1) of the NDPS Act and therefore, that the property cannot be used by anyone - including the petitioner - for commercial purposes.

He contends that the provisions of the NDPS Act are very clear that properties purchased out of ill-gotten wealth as a result of the nefarious actions under the said Act will have to be frozen and kept ready for confiscation and sale; and consequently, that the petitioner cannot be allowed to continue her business therein.
He, therefore, prays that this writ petition be dismissed.

5. The learned Standing Counsel appearing for the 1 st respondent - Adimali Grama Panchayat,
Sri.Latheesh Sebastian, submits that Ext.P11 has been issued only because Ext.P10 communication had been received by the Secretary of the Panchayat in March, 2019.

He says that, as is clear from Ext.P10, the property in question has been attached by the Assistant Excise Commissioner,
Thiruvananthapuram, under the provisions of the NDPS Act and therefore, that the petitioner cannot continue to do her business therein.

He says that therefore, through Ext.P11, she was offered Renjitha.K.M vs The Punchayath Secretary on 4 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52701782/
2 renewal of her Trade Licence, provided she is able to shift her business to WP(C).No.16393 OF 2019(Y) another premises.
He also, therefore, prays that this writ petition be dismissed.

6. When I consider the afore submissions and examine the materials on record, there is an additional reason why this Court is incapacitated from granting any relief to the petitioner, which is that Ext.P1 stated to be a lease agreement for a period of ten years, executed on Non Judicial Stamp Paper of Rs.150/- is not a registered document under the provisions of the applicable Statutes and Regulations.
Obviously, therefore, Ext.P1 is not a valid document and normally would be amenable to proceedings for impounding and resultant imposition of penalty.

Therefore, when the petitioner is thus unable to establish her rights over the property through a proper lease deed, I am certain that any order in this writ petition to direct the 1 st respondent - Grama Panchayat to renew her Trade Licence would be improper, if not wholly illegal.

This Court cannot, therefore, issue such an order;
and in any event of the matter, I do not find Ext.P11 to be in error since the Secretary of the Panchayat is absolutely right in maintaining that a Licence cannot be renewed for a WP(C).No.16393 OF 2019(Y) premises, which is now facing a proceedings under Section 68F(1) of the NDPS Act, particularly, when it is conceded before me that the aforementioned Sri.P.K.Shaji is a repeated offender.
In the afore circumstances, I cannot find this writ petition to be maintainable and therefore, dismiss it, however, without making any order as to costs.

SD/-
